body.statement: For every nonterminal normalized state refreshed by \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\), exactly one of the following cases is selected: an actually present supported-context selector occurrence; a nonempty set of nonancestors of the local outcome; a split into at least two explicitly computed districts; a canonically least reachable vertex with an inductively constructed positive-margin certificate; or a residual-ready state. In each of the first four cases the selected token is currently eligible, its exact local identity and positivity certificate are constructible by finite arithmetic, and the corresponding transition exists. After refreshing the successor agenda, \(\mu_H\) strictly decreases. Hence the fixed input-determined machine cannot stop before reaching a residual-ready state.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a normalized nonterminal state \(\zeta\). By \(\textnormal{ass:finite-categorical}\), every vertex alphabet, context list, graph, kernel circuit, and response table in \(\zeta\) is finite. Membership in \(H\), occurrence of a stored gate, ancestor and district computation, and the condition
\[
 \operatorname{dis}_{G_\zeta}(W)\cap
 \operatorname{de}_{G_\zeta}(W)=\{W\}
\tag{7}
\]
are therefore decidable by finite enumeration. Consequently \(\operatorname{Comp}_H\) executes one and only one branch of its ordered case definition. This already proves exhaustivity and mutual exclusivity of the five cases. We prove eligibility and progress in the four nonresidual cases.

Suppose first that \(\mathsf G(\zeta)\neq\varnothing\). Every member \((s,X,r,x_s)\) of this list is, by construction, an occurrence actually present in a labelled kernel and has \(s\in H\). At this occurrence the stored zero--one selector equation gives
\[
 X=x_s,
 \qquad
 \mathbf 1\{X=x\}=\mathbf 1\{x_s=x\}.
\tag{8}
\]
Thus substitution of \(x_s\) in its children is an exact polynomial identity modulo the gate-copy equations in \(\mathcal J\). The only initialization divisor is
\[
 q(S=s)=
 \sum_{v:(v,s)\in\mathcal C_H^{\mathrm{adm}}(G^+)}q(v,s)>0.
\tag{9}
\]
The sum is nonempty because \(s\in H\), and every summand indexed by an admissible cell is positive by \(\textnormal{ass:admissible-cell-interior}\). Hence the least selector token satisfies every eligibility clause of \(\textnormal{def:selector-transition}\). Rewriting one stored multiplexer cannot create another multiplexer occurrence, so the refreshed value of \(|\Sigma|\) is smaller by one. The first coordinate \(|R|\) is unchanged; therefore the corrected lexicographic measure, whose selector coordinate precedes both elimination and fixing work, decreases.

Now suppose \(\mathsf G(\zeta)=\varnothing\) and \(Z_\zeta\neq\varnothing\). By definition,
\[
 \varnothing\neq Z_\zeta
 \subseteq R_\zeta\setminus\operatorname{an}_{G_\zeta}(Y_\zeta).
\tag{10}
\]
The compiled token therefore passes the sum-elimination graphical test. Finite distributivity gives the exact successor identity
\[
 K'=\sum_{Z_\zeta}\prod_{k\in L}K_k.
\tag{11}
\]
Cross-multiplication after putting the finitely many rational factors over their registered common denominator proves the polynomial obligation. The successor removes the nonempty set \(Z_\zeta\) from the current random mask, so its first measure coordinate is strictly smaller.

Suppose next that (10) fails and \(|\mathsf D(\zeta)|>1\). Districts are the equivalence classes of bidirected connectivity and hence are explicitly computable and form a disjoint partition
\[
 R_\zeta=D_1\mathbin{\dot\cup}\cdots\mathbin{\dot\cup}D_j,
 \qquad j\ge 2,
 \qquad D_i\subsetneq R_\zeta.
\tag{12}
\]
The finite topological quotient of the predecessor kernel supplies the canonically ordered district factors. Multiplying those factors and cancelling only common numerator--denominator factors recovers the predecessor kernel; cross-multiplication is therefore an exact polynomial identity. Each child task is queried on all of \(D_i\), so it has no local nonancestor to remove, and its induced graph has the single district \(D_i\). Thus refreshing immediately after the split creates no replacement district token at the same random mask. The split consumes the sole \(\ell\)-token. Since the elimination coordinate precedes the fixing coordinate in \(\mu_H\), any fixing work exposed inside the child tasks occurs only in a later coordinate, and \(\mu_H\) decreases.

It remains to justify that a graphically reachable fixing is never blocked by an assumed certificate. Maintain the following invariant for each branch-reachable, structurally nonzero current kernel cell: it has a reduced representation
\[
 K_k=\frac{N_k}{D_k},
\tag{13}
\]
where \(D_k\) is a product of already registered positive entries and \(N_k\) is a finite positive-expression tree whose leaves are positive supported context cells and whose internal nodes are nonempty sums or products. At initialization, (13) follows from (9), with numerator \(q(v,s)>0\). Selector substitution only removes structurally impossible leaves and preserves (13) on the admissible cells. A finite sum or product combines the corresponding positive-expression trees. A preceding fixing or topological quotient appends its already verified positive divisor to \(D_k\). This proves (13) inductively for every current kernel.

For the least \(W\) satisfying (7), put the finitely many summands in
\[
 m_{s,W}=\sum_{x_W}K_{s,D}
\tag{14}
\]
over the common denominator \(D=\prod_{x_W}D_{x_W}\). Equations (13)--(14) give
\[
 m_{s,W}
 =\frac{
 \sum_{x_W}N_{x_W}\prod_{x'_W\ne x_W}D_{x'_W}}
 {\prod_{x_W}D_{x_W}}.
\tag{15}
\]
At least one summand is structurally admissible because a kernel is normalized on its finite alphabet. The numerator of (15) is consequently a nonempty sum of products of positive certified leaves, and its denominator is a product of earlier positive entries. The compiler constructs the tree in (15), expands both sides, and checks the identity coefficient by coefficient; it does not assume positivity. The frozen lemma \(\textnormal{lem:restricted-support-denominator-positivity}\) then implies \(m_{s,W}>0\) at every compatible observed law. Together with (7), this is precisely the required eligibility certificate for \(\textnormal{def:fixing-transition}\). Fixing removes \(W\) from the current random mask, so the first coordinate of \(\mu_H\) decreases.

For completeness, the positive-expression certificate in (15) has the stricter supported-margin form required by the fixing transition. The current kernel was obtained from an initialized supported-context kernel by a recorded valid fixing sequence and district restrictions. Since (7) makes \(W\) fixable, append \(W\) to that valid sequence and use \(\textnormal{lem:fixing-order-invariance}\) to move it to the next canonical position. In the resulting topological quotient, (14) is a conditional margin of the original context kernel, hence has the form
\[
 m_{s,W}
 =\frac{
 \sum_{v\in B_1}p_H(v,s)}
 {\prod_{j\in J}d_{H,j}},
 \qquad
 B_1\neq\varnothing,
\tag{15a}
\]
after cancellation, where \(B_1\) contains only cells compatible with the branch assignments and every \(d_{H,j}\) was registered earlier. This representation follows inductively from the topological quotient: marginalizing the next fixable variable replaces the current numerator by a marginal sum, while division appends its previously constructed conditional normalizer to the denominator registry. Equality of (15) and (15a) is checked by the same finite cross-multiplication. Thus the new numerator is a nonempty sum of supported admissible-cell probabilities and the inherited divisor is a product of earlier ledger entries; no broader positivity assertion is smuggled into eligibility.

If none of the four predicates holds, the displayed conjunction in \(\textnormal{def:initial-token-compiler}\) holds and, by definition, the state is residual-ready. Thus every nonresidual refreshed state has the asserted eligible successor and every such successor has smaller \(\mu_H\). A nonterminal stop before residual readiness is impossible.
